title: Introduction to Operation Properties
content: Operation properties are rules that describe how numbers behave when mathematical operations are performed. These properties help us simplify expressions, rearrange terms, and solve algebraic problems.
formula: Commutative, Associative, Identity, Inverse, and Distributive Properties
example: The expression 3 + 5 can be rewritten as 5 + 3 using the Commutative Property of Addition.

title: Commutative Property
content: The Commutative Property states that changing the order of numbers does not change the result. It applies to addition and multiplication but does not apply to subtraction or division.
formula:
a + b = b + a
a × b = b × a

title: Associative Property
content: The Associative Property states that changing the grouping of numbers does not change the result. It applies to addition and multiplication but does not apply to subtraction or division.
formula:
(a + b) + c = a + (b + c)
(a × b) × c = a × (b × c)

title: Identity Property
content: The Identity Property states that certain numbers can be combined with another number without changing its value. The additive identity is zero, while the multiplicative identity is one.

title: Inverse Property
content: The Inverse Property states that a number combined with its additive or multiplicative inverse produces the identity value. The additive inverse of a number is its opposite, while the multiplicative inverse is its reciprocal.

title: Distributive Property
content: The Distributive Property allows multiplication to be distributed across addition or subtraction inside parentheses. It is commonly used to expand and simplify algebraic expressions.
formula:
a(b + c) = ab + ac
a(b − c) = ab − ac

title: Applying Operation Properties
content: Operation properties can be combined to simplify expressions and make calculations easier. Identifying the correct property helps determine which transformation can be performed.
formula:
a + b = b + a → Commutative
a(b + c) = ab + ac → Distributive
example: 2(x + 5) can be simplified to 2x + 10 using the Distributive Property.
